JNJ.rationale: JNJ presents a mixed but mildly attractive picture. On the positive side, the company has a strong competitive position as the world's largest diversified healthcare company with two robust growth engines (Innovative Medicine and MedTech), a $100B revenue target for FY2026, and a long dividend track record. The Q1 2026 results showed solid operational growth of 6.4% with revenue of $24.1B and EPS of $2.14, and the company raised full-year guidance. The pipeline is progressing with FDA approval of ICOTYDE and strong performance from Darzalex and Tremfya. However, several factors temper enthusiasm: (1) Valuation has expanded significantly - the P/E has risen from ~17.5x a year ago to 30.1x currently, near the top of its 365-day range (17.2-31.1x), making it expensive vs its own history; (2) Net margins have compressed from 27.3% to 21.8% in recent quarters; (3) Operating cash flow was weak at $2.51B in the latest quarter vs $9.17B prior; (4) Significant headwinds persist including Stelara patent cliff, talc litigation (recent $32M verdict), FTC antitrust investigation, and potential Medicare pricing pressure. The stock has rallied ~67% from its 52-week low of $154.80 to $259.10, suggesting much of the positive narrative is already priced in. The upcoming Q2 earnings on July 15 could serve as a near-term catalyst, with consensus expecting $2.85 EPS and $25.05B revenue, but the 4.3% implied options move suggests the market is already positioned for this event.
